questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles expired feed entries? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What is the purpose of the random jitter added in put()?
choices: It makes feeds slightly different for each user
It stops many entries written at about the same moment from expiring simultaneously and causing a burst of rebuilds
It ensures the TTL is never shorter than configured, which cannot otherwise be guaranteed
It compensates for clock drift between servers

questions.prompt: An author with 2 million followers publishes a post. When do those followers see it in a feed that was cached before the post?
choices: Immediately, because onPostPublished invalidates all followers
After their cached feed expires, since fan-out invalidation is skipped above the follower limit
Never, until they follow the author again

questions.prompt: Two threads call getFeed for the same user whose entry has just expired. What happens?
choices: One thread blocks until the other finishes building the feed
Both build the feed and both put it; the last put wins and either result is a valid feed
An exception is thrown by ConcurrentHashMap
The feed is built once because put is atomic
